Shri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA for the State contends that the police authorities in compliance of the directions issued by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 46998 of 2020 (Junaid Vs State of U.P. and another) reported at 2021 (6) ADJ 511 and with a view to implement the provisions of POCSO Act, 2012 read with POCSO Rules, 2020, have served the bail application upon the victim/legal guardian as well as upon the CWC.

sentences.text:
By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
547 of 2023 at Police Station- Kotwali Nagar Mahoba, District-Mahoba under Sections 452,
376(AB), 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.

entities.text: Police Station- Kotwali Nagar Mahoba, District-Mahoba
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 06.01.2024.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 20.11.2023.

The following arguments made by Ms. Priyanka Devi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Yatish Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel on behalf of the informant and Shri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor in the prosecution case only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2. The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim is in fact a major.
3. Delay in institution of proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
4. The applicant is the second husband of the victim's mother.
5. The FIR is a result of the matrimonial dispute between the applicant and the victim's mother.
6. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim against the applicant at the behest of her mother.
The victim is a child who was tutored by her mother to falsely implicate the applicant.
The said witness is not reliable.
7. The medical examination of the victim was got conducted two months after the incident.
The medical report cannot be connected with the offence.
8. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
9. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

sentences.text: In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Narayan Datt Chansauriya be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number,
on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 16.5.2024
